_what: Baselines for bench/import-target/measure.mjs (#2877 go, #2878 csharp, #2879 dart, #2880 ruby).
_fingerprint_note: Per-language sha256 over every distinct fromFile|target -> resolved target. A change here is a BEHAVIOUR change: the resolver returned a different target set. Re-baseline only with a deliberate resolution change, and only after test/unit/scope-resolution/import-target-index-parity.test.ts has been updated to match — that harness, not this file, is what proves a rewrite preserved the tie-breaks.
_scaling_note: Measured on this branch at the full 400/1600 scale: go 0.98, csharp 1.08, dart 1.09, ruby 1.12. The same corpus scored 3.36 / 4.10 / 3.32 / 3.87 against the pre-#2877 scans at 150/600, matching the ratios reported in the issues. The 1.8 budget sits well above the linear result and well below the quadratic one; the timing arm is the only one that can move under CI load, so re-run on an idle machine before investigating a ratio failure.
_shape_note: files/imports/resolved/distinct_outcomes are asserted exactly. A fingerprint alone cannot tell a legitimate resolution change from a corpus that was quietly shrunk below the size at which the scaling arm can see anything.
